subject: Custody guarantees, onshore KMS, and non-learning evidence request
body:
From: Anjali Rao <anjali@medguard.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.example.com>
Cc: MedGuard Legal <legal@medguard.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions: no-training commitment + KMS onshore routing

Hi David,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile. Before procurement sign-off our legal and security teams raised two items we need clarified in the DPA and ops playbook:

1) Non-learning / no-training commitment: we need an auditable assertion that MedGuard tenant interactions will not be used to improve public or internal models (no adaptive training). Can you provide the exact clause language you can commit to, and the operational proof you will provide during onboarding?

2) Onshore key management: because we process patient-adjacent data, we need keys for our tenant to be held in a US-only KMS and ensure model-serving instances that handle our traffic use onshore KMS wrapping. We’d like a short architecture diagram and a sample audit log extract showing KMS key creation and usage tied to a tenant id.

If you can send a short deliverable list and an ETA, that would be helpful. We expect this to be part of the SOW and DPA exhibit.

Best,
Anjali Rao
Head of Security & Privacy
MedGuard

---
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.example.com>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@medguard.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.example.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions: no-training commitment + KMS onshore routing

Hi Anjali — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then an action plan below:

- No-training commitment: Redwood can commit to a per-tenant non-training flag that prevents tenant data from being allowed into model improvement pipelines. We can include this as a DPA exhibit clause: "Redwood will not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve models that may be accessible to third parties." We will also provide an attestation document and an operational checklist during onboarding.

- Onshore KMS & evidence: We support tenant-specific CMKs in a US-only KMS region (customer-managed KMS via Bring-Your-Own-Key or Redwood-managed but region-locked). We will provide an architecture diagram and an audit log sample that redacts tenant PII but shows key creation, ACLs, and crypto-op events tied to the tenant id.

Action plan and deliverables (we can have these as attachments / exhibit in the DPA):
1) Draft DPA exhibit with the no-training clause + sample language for prompt/response ownership and derivative restrictions (deliverable: dpa_exhibit_no_training_v1.docx) — owner: Kimberly — ETA: 2026-09-04
2) Onshore KMS design diagram (deliverable: redwood_onshore_kms_diagram.pdf) — owner: Marissa — ETA: 2026-09-03
3) Operational evidence pack (audit-log-sample.csv + no-learn-attestation-template.docx) showing: key creation event, tenant-tagged crypto ops, and a signed attestation confirming the tenant flag prevents learning pipelines from ingesting data — owner: David — ETA: 2026-09-06

I’ve looped in Marissa and Kim to prepare the technical artifacts and the draft clause. If MedGuard legal wants exact DPA text, we can provision an editable exhibit for negotiation.

Regards,
David
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.example.com>, Anjali Rao <anjali@medguard.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.example.com>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.example.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 13:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions: no-training commitment + KMS onshore routing

Anjali — attaching the diagram we’ll hand to MedGuard. A few implementation notes inline:

- Tenant CMKs: We can provision a customer-supplied CMK in the US-east KMS zone and ensure all inference nodes handling tenant traffic decrypt/wrap with that CMK before any ephemeral caching layer writes to disk.
- Serve-time encryption: Keys never leave the US region; we use per-request wrapping to avoid storing raw tenant secrets on GPU nodes.
- Auditability: We can provide a filtered CSV of CloudKMS events (audit-log-sample.csv) with a tenant_id column. We’ll redact any patient identifiers but preserve timestamps, event types (CreateKey, Decrypt, WrapKey), and the principal performing the operation.
- Fallback model routing: If onshore capacity is constrained we can route to a compatible model variant in the same region (no cross-border route) with an explicit SLA and failover policy documented in the SOW.

Also noted: MedGuard asked about prompt/response ownership. Kimberly and I recommend the DPA exhibit include both: (a) non-training guarantee and (b) explicit ownership/derivative rights language stating that customer retains ownership of prompts and responses and Redwood obtains no IP in customer-provided prompts or generated outputs beyond delivering service.

Attaching: redwood_onshore_kms_diagram.pdf, audit-log-sample.csv

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.example.com>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@medguard.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions: no-training commitment + KMS onshore routing

Hi Anjali — drafting suggested clause below; this is a candidate DPA exhibit paragraph for your review. We can iterate wording: please mark any redlines.

Proposed DPA exhibit text (draft):

"Non-Training and Ownership of Customer Interactions.
(a) Redwood will not use Customer Data, including prompts, inputs, and responses, to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve models that are available to or shared with other customers or the general public, except with the Customer’s prior written consent.
(b) Customer retains all rights, title, and interest in Customer Data and in outputs generated from Customer Data. Redwood disclaims any ownership of Customer prompts and generated outputs; Redwood’s rights are solely limited to performing the services described in the Agreement.
(c) Evidence and Auditability: Upon Customer request during onboarding and as otherwise agreed in the SOW, Redwood will provide a one-time attestation and an operational evidence packet that includes an architecture diagram, a filtered audit log extract demonstrating KMS events tied to the Customer’s tenant id, and a signed statement from Redwood’s privacy team confirming the non-training flag is in effect for the Customer’s tenant."

If this looks good to start, I’ll turn it into redline-ready language and send via DocuSign link for signature.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Lead Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference

---
Notes / next steps:
- Kimberly to produce redlineable exhibit (file: no-learn-attestation-template.docx) by 2026-09-04.
- Marissa to deliver final onshore KMS diagram and filtered audit sample by 2026-09-03.
- David to assemble the operational evidence pack and coordinate a 30-min call with MedGuard security the week of 2026-09-07 to review the artifacts.

Attachments referenced in-thread: redwood_onshore_kms_diagram.pdf (diagram), audit-log-sample.csv (filtered events), no-learn-attestation-template.docx (draft clause template).

----
Forwarding note: This thread should be included in the SOW exhibit and the procurement package. Connor — please add the deliverables above to the procurement checklist and create a provisioning ticket that maps tenant id MG-2026-07-45 to KMS key id once MedGuard signs the SOW.
